doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Gil Evans, Birth of the Cool and the Second Herd
title: Gil's basement apartment and the Thornhill band
summary: Mandel describes the basement apartment behind the Chinese laundry as a round-the-clock musical den, and Gil's Thornhill band and its players.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: So did you hang out a lot with all those people who hung out in his apartment?
Yep, behind the Chinese laundry, exactly, below the Chinese laundry.
It was a basement apartment, yeah.

Kind of dank and airless, but who cares, it went twenty-four hours a day, music played, Gil was a bachelor, he had nobody living with him but a cat named Becky. And we were there, you know he was sort of like a big den mother, he loved being with the younger guys, he didn’t care about at all with being with his contemporaries, which was another generation really. And he was anything but a father figure.
He said of that period, I guess, that he wanted what he called, “musical companionship,” because he said he hadn’t had much of it.

Yeah, he sure did, he wanted musical companionship and he wanted to hear what everybody had to say. That’s the way Gil was, he was one of the most giving individuals I think I ever met, just of himself and of letting everything in, wanting everything in new. He was still writing for Claude [Thornhill] and he was doing all those… you know incorporating bop into the band, and it was a good band, people like Gene Williams was in the band singing, it was a good band.
Yeah, Lee Konitz. He had some…
Yeah, right, Barry, Billy Exner, he had…
Joel Shulman was the bass player.

Joel Shulman, right, good bass player he was. He was with Buddy Rich’s first band with me too, I forgot about him. Great bass player. Had a wonderful big round sound, he had just come back from being overseas with the premier Glenn Miller Orchestra, in the army band along with all those guys, you know.
I read somewhere a nice story about Thornhill’s rhythm section with Gil instead of Claude would rent studio time up at Nola’s and just go up there and do nothing but play time.

We used to do that all the time, I mean I didn’t do it with those guys but we spent our lives up at Nola’s, just paying for rooms and rehearsing. Or having sessions, we’d rent a room and have a session.
